title: Genome-Factory: A Library for Tuning, Deploying, and Interpreting Genomic Foundation Models
claim: A unified toolkit decomposes the whole development workflow into modular, interoperable components that connect from data through to interpretation.
layout: 6 color-coded module boxes in a 3-column grid, left-to-right arrows
description: A block diagram with six rounded, color-coded module boxes. Each box has a tab-style title and smaller sub-boxes inside. The left column holds Genome Collector (blue), with Data Acquisition and Data Preprocessing, and Model Loader (orange), with Tokenizer Loading and Model Loading. The center column holds Model Trainer (green), with a 2x2 grid of Workflow Configuration, Parameter Optimization, Model Adaptation and Training Execution, and Inference Engine (pink). The Inference Engine has Embedding Extraction → Extracted Embedding and Sequence Generation → Generated Sequence. The right column holds Benchmarker (purple), with Standard Benchmark and Custom Benchmark, and Biological Interpreter (magenta), with Sparse Auto-encoder. Black arrows run left to right: Collector and Loader feed the Trainer, Loader feeds Inference, Trainer feeds Benchmarker, and Inference feeds Interpreter. The color-coded titles draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of GENOME-FACTORY. The framework consists of six components. Genome Collector acquires genomic sequences from public repositories and performs preprocessing (e.g., GC normalization). Model Loader supports major genomic models (e.g., HyenaDNA, DNABERT-2, Caduceus, Nucleotide Transformer, EVO and GenomeOcean) and their tokenizers. Model Trainer configures workflows, adapts models to classification or regression tasks, and executes training with full fine-tuning or parameter-efficient methods (LoRA, adapters). Inference Engine enables embedding extraction and sequence generation. Benchmarker provides standard benchmarks and allows integration of custom tasks. Biological Interpreter enhances interpretability through sparse auto-encoders.
abstract: We introduce Genome-Factory, the first integrated Python library for tuning, deploying, and interpreting genomic foundation models. Our core contribution is to simplify and unify the workflow for genomic model development: data collection, model tuning, inference, benchmarking, and interpretability. For data collection, Genome-Factory offers an automated pipeline to download genomic sequences and preprocess them. For model tuning, Genome-Factory supports both full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning across diverse genomic models. For inference, Genome-Factory enables both embedding extraction and DNA sequence generation. For benchmarking, we include two existing benchmarks and provide a flexible interface to incorporate additional benchmarks. For interpretability, Genome-Factory introduces an open-source biological interpreter based on a sparse auto-encoder. We validate the utility of Genome-Factory across three dimensions: (i) Compatibility with diverse models and fine-tuning methods; (ii) Benchmarking downstream performance using two open-source benchmarks; (iii) Biological interpretation of learned representations with DNABERT-2. These results highlight its practical value for real-world genomic analysis. GitHub: https://github.com/WeiminWu2000/Genome_Factory.
